validity.researcher_notes: This row's LengthKnownKm=14202.00 (=8,824 mi) matches TETCO's well-documented ~9,000-mile, wholly-domestic Gulf-Coast-Texas/Louisiana-to-New-York-City system, confirming the row is an aggregated whole-network route rather than one segment. No independent source describes TETCO (Enbridge-owned since the 2017 Spectra merger) as having any facility in Mexico -- its own Wikipedia overview (which I read only for the network's geographic description, not as a route ref) describes it purely as a Texas/Louisiana-to-NYC domestic system with no Mexico leg. TETCO's southernmost well-documented receipt/hub point is the Agua Dulce Hub in Nueces County, TX (~27.78N), roughly 130 miles north of the Rio Grande border (~26.0N at the coast) -- there is no TETCO infrastructure reported anywhere near the border. (Separately, TETCO-affiliated projects that DO reach toward Mexico -- the Pomelo Connector interconnect to Valley Crossing Pipeline near Agua Dulce, and the Valley Crossing border crossing itself near Brownsville -- are DIFFERENT companies'/projects' facilities, not TETCO Main Line, and don't extend TETCO itself to the border.) Given RouteAccuracy=high but a landfall of only 4.7 km, the far more likely explanation is a coastline/political-boundary polygon simplification artifact in the underlying GIS boundary layer (a common source of small false country-crossings on Gulf-coast and river-border pipelines) rather than a genuine TETCO presence in Mexico. This is a route-geometry question, not a row-attribute error, so no [ref]/value fill applies -- flagging for a routes-repo geometry look per standing rule 8 (never propose new coordinates from this leg).
